correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary cases are handled. Cubic units in \(\mathbb Z_3\) are exactly +/-1 mod9 by the explicitly Hensel-liftable map t+3t²+3t³. For αx³+3βy³ the unit-value surjection and value 3β give quotient valuations 0,+/-1; scaling by \(27\) covers all integer valuations. For αx³+βy³ either a unit isotropic root produces the entire ideal 9\(\mathbb Z_3\), yielding every quotient by scaling a nonzero value, or a noncube unit ratio produces all of \(3U\) by a derivative-unit Hensel map and oddness. Coefficient valuations reduce by integral variable scaling to these cases, and integer-coordinate density follows from continuity and Z dense in \(\mathbb Z_3\). The independent standard-library finite checker confirms 3-adic local residue assertions in 108 and 36 cases and 6400 exact normalization identities; it is explicitly not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The general coefficient-uniform prime-three density theorem is not given in the most relevant inspected sources. Theorem 1.2(1),(3) of the 2021 Antony--Barman manuscript and Theorem 1.1(1),(3) of the 2022 extension state non-density for some cases now proved dense, so these do not subsume this theorem and in fact present incompatible predictions at \(p=3\). The 2018 unweighted two-cubes theorem is a strict specialization; no fixed-coefficient implication covers all nonzero a,b. Searches of mathematical research records with exact formulas and aliases yielded no equivalent published record. This supports novelty only within searched evidence and does not establish bibliographic priority.

value.rationale: The universal binary cubic quotient density classification at the bad prime \(p=3\) removes every restriction on nonzero coefficients, settling a natural entire parameter family and repairing the mathematical boundary predicted by two published preprint theorem statements. This is motivated by an existing direct classification problem and does not amount to a textbook substitution or arbitrary finite special-case census. The exact 3-adic realization strengthens the integer-density statement and gives a new simple explanation of the ramified-prime exception. The multivariable restriction follows naturally but is not counted as an independent finding.
